method: Whole-file manual reading of MainFrame.h; pinned bytes verified. No Windows command execution.
findings: Main-frame routes connect close/end-session/destroy/timer and synchronous callback messages to previously reviewed implementations. Taskbar creation uses registered message. Presence of a route is not proof handler succeeds at runtime.

Logical focus distinguishes file, duplicate, top, search, watcher, permissions, extension and analytics views; inline view switches select appropriate existing tabs. View getters dereference borrowed tabbed-view pointer without independent null guard; valid frame construction remains precondition.

Frame owns embedded splitter/status/toolbar/progress controls but retains borrowed pointers to pane instances and working CItem. Clear/teardown sequencing, not header ownership, determines pointer validity.
Cleanup result future and jthread are members, with cached four counters. Explicit shutdown join was reviewed in MainFrame.cpp; declaration alone does not establish cancellation or timeout.
Splitter storage pointers reference persisted option storage; SetStorage dereferences supplied pointer and only regards strictly0..1as user ratio. No null/finite contract enforcement in this setter.
Settings sheet snapshots initial dark-mode/language values and computes restart request against them. Request flag and actual restart outcome remain distinct.
Watcher-filter paint handler is routed for WM_NCPAINT, WM_PAINT and WM_PRINT; actual paint and invalid-regex behavior remains in unreviewed MainFrame.Commands.cpp.

Tool command ranges cover shadow-copy/defrag/checkdisk and UI scaling; update routes are distinct from execution routes. Numeric range disjointness and authorization behavior are not established by declaration reading.
limits: No UI command, resource-ID overlap, pointer-lifetime, focus, paint or cleanup-thread runtime tests performed.
No foreign production code adopted; native pHash investigation deferred. Global completed repository count remains147/500.
